blindSummary:
This is a low-danger destination for transgender visitors. Legal gender recognition has worked by self-declaration since January 2022 — a personal declaration before the civil registrar, with no court or medical requirements (binary male/female only; no non-binary marker). Same-sex marriage has been legal since 2022 (approved by referendum), a gender-neutral rape law took effect in 2024, and employers have a legal duty of care toward trans employees. General crime is exceptionally low.

The notable legislative shortcoming — flagged by a regional legal-rights index and by the government's own review — is that the criminal hate-crime and hate-speech provision covers sexual orientation but not gender identity. So a person targeted specifically for being trans does not benefit from that aggravation in criminal law, though the protections available through employment and constitutional law are broader. Reported hate crimes against LGBTIQ people have risen about fivefold since 2020 (around six per week, but from a low absolute base of ~309 cases in 2024).

The federal government adopted the country's first national action plan against LGBTIQ hate crime in January 2026 (running to 2030), signalling a pro-trans institutional direction. There is no rollback movement.
blindOutOfScope: This country's principal travel risks (mountain hazards, road safety) affect all travellers.
blindSourceSummaries: Official page of the federal gender-equality office: since 1 July 2020, public incitement to hatred/discrimination based on sexual orientation is punishable under the criminal code's anti-discrimination provision; 'marriage for all' equality in force since 1 July 2022; covers LGBTIQ rights developments.

Technical-university page on gender identity in the civil status register: since 1 January 2022, any person registered in a municipality here may change their sex marker and/or first name by personal declaration before a civil registrar - no court or medical requirement; changes are generally limited to binary categories, with some regional variation.
A public broadcaster's international service: hundreds of people in this country have changed their legal gender using the simplified self-declaration process introduced in 2022.
The same international service: this country records roughly six hate crimes per week against LGBTIQ people (based on monitoring reports).

Federal gender-equality office: on 28 January 2026 the national government adopted the first National Action Plan to combat hate crimes against LGBTIQ persons 2026-2030, with three pillars - victim support and protection, prevention, and monitoring of violence.
Public broadcaster's international service coverage of the same first national action plan against anti-LGBTIQ hate crimes (2026).

Legal-information platform overview (June 2026): marriage equality since July 2022 (64.1% referendum approval); criminal-law protection against sexual-orientation discrimination since 2020; streamlined legal gender change since January 2022. Notes gaps: gender identity is not fully covered by the criminal anti-discrimination provision, and conversion therapy and surrogacy remain unregulated.

Trans-support workplace platform: the legal framework for trans people at work here - employers' duty of care under the code of obligations and the equality act; employees may use their preferred name and gender at work without official change; employers must keep trans identity confidential; solutions for showers/toilets/cloakrooms must respect everyone's personal rights; the trans person may wear service clothing matching their gender identity.
A country page on a regional LGBTI legal-equality index: this country's overall score and per-category compliance breakdown, following its 2021 votes on self-determination and anti-discrimination.

Regional security organisation's 2024 hate-crime report for this country: the country regularly reports hate-crime data; the criminal code has no general hate-crime provision - hate crimes are addressed under anti-discrimination provisions; the organisation notes recording does not sufficiently distinguish hate crimes and police do not record bias motivation.

A UN refugee agency's country page: everyone in this country has the right to equal treatment; discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity is prohibited; LGBTIQ+ people enjoy equal rights; same-sex couples can marry since 1 July 2022; lists reporting mechanisms and support organisations.
blindLocalsOnly: The self-declaration legal-gender-recognition process (binary only, no non-binary marker) and the employer duty of care are resident-facing administrative/employment law.
blindTangential: Same-sex marriage legal since 2022 — relevant to trans visitors travelling with partners.
